releases.title: Open the wiki from the main menu
releases.summary: A Wiki button is available directly below Time to Fight, with an external-browser request that keeps the game page open.
evidence: Based on production commit b5be3892f62909f7a8e7dc0c7a0b2b0a3dc15f29 and game build steel-tape-auth-ad27047a6f73.
The existing menu UI asset adds the link; the game engine page and save format are preserved. The service-worker asset-cache revision changes so reloaded installed games receive the new menu asset.
Android intent syntax follows https://developer.chrome.com/docs/android/intents. Installed-web-app behavior remains controlled by the device and browser.

sections.title: A wiki button on the game menu
items: A clearly labelled Wiki button appears directly below Time to Fight. It uses the existing menu styling, supports keyboard and controller focus, and links to the full player wiki on the live server.
The link opens a new browsing context with opener access disabled, so it does not replace the current game page.

The existing game UI script supplies the button and guards against duplicate insertion. Cached UI assets receive a new service-worker cache revision; an already running game may need a reload or restart to show the button.

sections.title: Opening outside the installed game
items: On Android in standalone, fullscreen or minimal-UI display mode, the button requests Chrome through an Android browser intent. An HTTPS fallback is included if the intent cannot be handled.
Other environments use a standard HTTPS link with target=_blank and rel=external, noopener and noreferrer. This requests a separate browser window or tab and keeps the game page open.

A website cannot universally force a particular external browser or override every installed-app, operating-system or embedded-browser policy. Device handoff is therefore best effort, rather than a promise that every platform will leave its app container.

sections.title: Scope and validation
items: This release adds menu navigation. It changes no combat values, progression, costs, XP, rewards, player saves or public game-content entries.
The embedded engine build remains steel-tape-auth-ad27047a6f73; this is a separate UI-asset/cache revision.
The owner requested a silent update. No Discord announcement is sent for this release.

knownIssues: Actual Android/iOS app-to-browser handoff has not been tested on a physical device. Native new-window behavior and generated Android intent/fallback paths are covered by browser automation.
If Chrome is unavailable or the host blocks external launches, the operating system/browser decides how to handle the HTTPS fallback.
validation: Main-menu link placement and usable target size checked at desktop, landscape-phone and portrait-phone dimensions.
Native new-window opening, null opener and preservation of the original game page checked in browser automation.
Standalone/fullscreen Android intent construction, HTTPS fallback, duplicate protection and the iOS standalone link path checked with simulated environments.

releases.title: A field guide that feels at home on your phone
releases.summary: A refreshed interface with easier phone navigation, typo-tolerant search, saved entries, two reading themes and better tools for long articles.
evidence: Compared with production commit 48da0e78d013dcbc2eba8d783102bd79786acb7d, gameplay build steel-tape-auth-ad27047a6f73.
Fuse.js 7.5.0 and a 29-icon Lucide Static 1.57.0 subset are pinned, served locally, and accompanied by their license files and vendor hashes.
Declared typography values compared with the previous production wiki CSS. Percentages describe CSS font-size changes, not gameplay or measured player outcomes.

sections.title: Made for phone navigation
items: A compact sticky header and a dedicated navigation drawer replace the horizontal category strip on narrow screens. The drawer exposes every database category and the link back to the game.
A bottom navigation bar keeps Explore, Search, Updates and Saved within reach. Controls account for the phone's bottom safe area, and the page reserves room beneath the content.
Cards, quick facts, article layouts and dialogs adjust to narrow phones, tablets and desktop windows. Wide numerical patch-note tables remain scrollable, with an explanatory hint and keyboard focus.

sections.title: Find an entry even when the spelling is imperfect
items: Fuse.js adds typo-tolerant matching to the wiki search. Exact matches are retained, while additional close matches help with misspelled names and multi-word queries.

A site-wide search dialog is available from any article, using the header button, the phone's Search tab, or Ctrl+K / Command+K. The slash shortcut focuses the current page's search when available and opens site search elsewhere.

Arrow keys move through site-search suggestions, Enter opens a focused entry, and Escape dismisses the dialog. Search, icons and their supporting library files are served by the game server; no external search service receives queries.

sections.title: Keep your own useful pages
items: Every database article has a Save entry control. Saved entries have their own page, persist across reloads on the same browser and can be removed individually or cleared.

The home page can show recently opened articles so a player can return to a quest, ingredient or location. Recent and saved pages are stored locally in this browser; they do not sync with a game account or another device.
Copy page link shares an entry or the canonical full-release URL. If clipboard access is unavailable, the interface opens a selectable link for manual copying.

sections.title: Reading, themes and long-page tools
items: The visual refresh uses a forest-and-brass dark palette, a parchment light palette, consistent Lucide icons, clearer cards, rounded surfaces and more consistent spacing.
The theme switch stores the reader's choice in this browser. Larger article and result text improves the default reading scale; browser zoom remains available.
Long articles and release notes gain an On this page section list. The list can be collapsed on phones, and its buttons move keyboard focus to the chosen heading.

A reading progress line and a back-to-top control help with longer pages. Reduced-motion preferences disable animated transitions and smooth scrolling. Native dialogs provide focus containment and Escape handling.

metrics.name: Quest chapter paragraph and objective font size
metrics.context: Default declared chapter copy and objective size in the wiki; this is a typography change, not a gameplay change.

metrics.name: Search result title font size
metrics.context: Default declared title size in the standard results list.

metrics.name: Search result description font size
metrics.context: Default declared summary size in standard page search results; compact dialog suggestions may use a smaller summary.

sections.title: Compatibility, scope and verification
items: This release changes the wiki interface. The game page, game build, saves, combat, costs, XP, rewards and existing release records are preserved.
The public catalogue remains subject to its existing review policy. Secrets, discovery clues, hidden content and private player data are not added by these interface features.

Interactive preferences rely on browser storage. If storage is unavailable, the current page still works but saved entries and preferences cannot be retained. Saved pages are specific to the current browser and origin.
Search dialogs use the browser's native dialog support. Font fallbacks remain available if the optional web fonts cannot load. No measured speed or frame-rate gain is claimed.

knownIssues: Saved entries, recent pages and theme preferences do not sync across browsers or devices.
The existing guide coverage gaps remain: this interface update does not add unverified gameplay content.
validation: Responsive interface checks at 320, 390, 768 and 1440 CSS pixels, including dark and light themes and horizontal-overflow checks.
Checks cover typo-tolerant search, search keyboard navigation, drawer dismissal, saved-entry persistence/removal, theme persistence, article jump links, Escape dismissal and reduced-motion behavior.
Existing catalogue, quest-link, recipe, release arithmetic, archive, exported-subfolder and service-worker checks remain part of the release gate.

releases.title: A live reference and permanent full patch notes
releases.summary: The player reference is checked against the current game, with permanent detailed release pages and clearer release timestamps.
evidence: Verified production gameplay build steel-tape-auth-ad27047a6f73 at commit 0e44bd249c19314bb661eb7271bc02048db5e2df before this wiki-only update.
Live-source refresh verified 229 public entries, no changed entries and no new pending entries. Gameplay files are preserved byte-for-byte.

sections.title: The current player reference
items: The wiki was refreshed from the actual live game. Its 229 reviewed public entries and their player-facing values were unchanged in this refresh.

Quest chapters, prerequisites, objectives, ordinary rewards, people and places, gathering requirements, recipes, equipment and combat perks remain searchable and linked. No new gameplay system is claimed by this release.

sections.title: Detailed release records
items: The patch-note archive keeps permanent links for individual releases, including this page. Existing release entries remain intact. Factual corrections will be published as new records identifying the earlier claim.
Release facts now display the release time with the date and timezone. Search and direct release links continue to work from the wiki subfolder.

Full notes accompany future game updates and explain affected modes, conditions, mechanics, fixes, interactions, edge cases, compatibility and known issues. The short Discord announcement points to the complete public record.

sections.title: Understanding numerical changes
items: Future numerical changes use verified old and new values, explicit units, the absolute difference and the relative percentage change. Percentage-valued statistics also show percentage-point differences.

A zero baseline has no defined relative percentage change. Unknown old values are identified as unknown rather than guessed. Source constants and calculated percentages do not establish measured performance or win-rate improvements.

This release changes the wiki and release workflow. It does not change gameplay balance, costs, XP, ordinary rewards, cooldowns, probabilities, save formats or controls; there are no numerical gameplay deltas to report.

sections.title: Compatibility and verification
items: The current gameplay build is retained, including the latest fixes already present in production. No player-save migration is required for this wiki update.
The wiki and full notes remain under the live game domain. Wiki requests use the existing network-only behavior rather than the game offline cache.
Content, link, numeric-note and desktop/phone browser checks cover the reference and full-note pages. No measured frame-rate or loading-speed improvement is claimed.

knownIssues: Coverage is still incomplete for public cosmetics, housing, full mode walkthroughs, detailed controls and advanced squire care. The coverage page continues to identify these gaps.
Physical Android and real-account multi-device gameplay acceptance are outside this wiki-only verification.
validation: Live-source extraction: matching production build, 229 reviewed entries, no pending additions and no catalogue changes.
Release archive preserves the earlier wiki-launch record and its permanent URL.

releases.title: The Steel & Tape player wiki is here
releases.summary: A searchable player reference and a permanent home for detailed patch notes, hosted alongside the live game.
evidence: Verified current production game build steel-tape-auth-ad27047a6f73, Git commit 5a888e39016e6034cb0b0d7ca10cb4110044ce14. The wiki release preserves that gameplay build.
229-entry public catalogue validated with 88 quest chapters; desktop and phone browser checks passed

sections.title: The player database
items: 22 questlines contain 88 chapters, with prerequisites, objectives, gold and XP rewards, dialogue choices and follow-up quests.
10 public regions and 10 arenas link to 67 people and services. Region pages include world coordinates, access requirements and regional gathering information.
The first catalogue includes 17 standard equipment pieces, 19 materials, 6 trades, 45 combat perks, 22 core crafting recipes, 4 repeatable contracts and 5 fighter archetypes.
Search supports names, objectives, ingredients, places and other entry details. Articles link to related quests, NPCs, materials and prerequisites.

sections.title: A home for full patch notes
items: Detailed release pages live at /wiki/patch-notes/ and have permanent release links for Discord announcements.
Future balance notes must state the old and new values, units, exact absolute change and calculated relative percentage change. Changes to percentage-valued stats must also state percentage points.

Full notes can include mechanics, edge cases, affected modes, progression, crafting costs, world changes, interface changes, performance measurements, fixes, known issues and validation that cannot fit comfortably in a Discord announcement.
No game balance values were changed by the wiki launch. There is no verified previous-game comparison attached to this entry, so it claims no historical buffs, nerfs or percentage changes.

sections.title: Hosting and keeping pages current
items: The wiki is served from the live game’s /wiki/ subfolder. The game remains at the root URL.
The game service worker bypasses wiki requests so a cached game page cannot replace a wiki page, and wiki assets are fetched fresh.
The deployment handoff requires reviewed wiki updates and full release notes after successful live releases, then a concise Discord announcement containing the exact full-notes URL.
Secrets, hidden locations, secret rewards, triggers, discovery clues, private player data and admin tools stay out of both wiki entries and patch notes.

sections.title: Known coverage gaps
items: Public cosmetics, housing, complete mode walkthroughs, detailed controls, advanced squire care and other systems still need expanded guides.
This launch starts the detailed public release archive. Older game releases are not reconstructed from memory or presented as measured numerical comparisons.

knownIssues: Some public game systems still need fuller guide coverage; see Sources & coverage.
validation: Content checks validate quest links, prerequisites, crafting ingredients and unique entry IDs.
Browser verification covers desktop and phone layouts, search, every article, region navigation and patch-note pages.
